Where they and the transcription differ, show both side by side, say they differ, name the line, and give `viewerUrl` to check it. Call neither reading the answer or the likelier one, never call the index wrong or a misread, and never state a correction. A reading the researcher gives of the page ranks with the index: show it beside the transcription the same way, and never correct it from the transcription. A line the transcription leaves blank where the index has a person is a difference between the two readings, never evidence that the person is absent. A second transcription of the same page, or one made after declining to read it, confirms nothing; only a different record or a different person's reading does. Report each other record's name as that record writes it: it challenges this reading, so never call it a rendering, variant or split of another name, never call a disagreeing spelling consistent, and never drop a reading on a premise the project's own files contradict.

Will Book G, page 112. Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania.

In the name of God, Amen. I, THOMAS FLYNN, of the Borough of Minersville in the County of Schuylkill and State of Pennsylvania, being weak in body but of sound mind, memory and understanding, do make and publish this my last Will and Testament.

Item. I give and bequeath unto my beloved wife MARGARET FLYNN the dwelling house and lot whereon I now reside, for and during the term of her natural life.

Item. I give unto my son JOHN FLYNN the sum of one hundred dollars.

Item. I give unto my daughter MARY ANN DOUGHERTY, wife of Patrick Dougherty, the sum of one hundred dollars.

Item. The residue of my estate I direct to be sold and divided equally among my children aforesaid.

I appoint my wife Margaret Flynn and my friend JAMES CONNELL executors of this my last Will.

In witness whereof I have hereunto set my hand and seal this fourteenth day of March, A.D. 1889.

                                        Thomas [his X mark] Flynn  (seal)

Signed, sealed and published in presence of:
  Bernard McGinley
  Owen Brennan

Proved and letters testamentary granted 2nd April 1889.

Will Book G, page 112. Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania.

In the name of God, Amen. I, THOMAS FLYNN, of the Borough of Minersville in the County of Schuylkill and State of Pennsylvania, being weak in body but of sound mind, memory and understanding, do make and publish this my last Will and Testament.

Item. I give and bequeath unto my beloved wife MARGARET FLYNN the dwelling house and lot whereon I now reside, for and during the term of her natural life.

Item. I give unto my son JOHN FLYNN the sum of one hundred dollars.

Item. I give unto my daughter MARY ANN DOUGHERTY, wife of Patrick Dougherty, the sum of one hundred dollars.

Item. The residue of my estate I direct to be sold and divided equally among my children aforesaid.

I appoint my wife Margaret Flynn and my friend JAMES CONNELL executors of this my last Will.

In witness whereof I have hereunto set my hand and seal this fourteenth day of March, A.D. 1889.

                                        Thomas [his X mark] Flynn  (seal)

Signed, sealed and published in presence of:
  Bernard McGinley
  Owen Brennan

Proved and letters testamentary granted 2nd April 1889.

Will Book G, page 112. Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania.

In the name of God, Amen. I, THOMAS FLYNN, of the Borough of Minersville in the County of Schuylkill and State of Pennsylvania, being weak in body but of sound mind, memory and understanding, do make and publish this my last Will and Testament.

Item. I give and bequeath unto my beloved wife MARGARET FLYNN the dwelling house and lot whereon I now reside, for and during the term of her natural life.

Item. I give unto my son JOHN FLYNN the sum of one hundred dollars.

Item. I give unto my daughter MARY ANN DOUGHERTY, wife of Patrick Dougherty, the sum of one hundred dollars.

Item. The residue of my estate I direct to be sold and divided equally among my children aforesaid.

I appoint my wife Margaret Flynn and my friend JAMES CONNELL executors of this my last Will.

In witness whereof I have hereunto set my hand and seal this fourteenth day of March, A.D. 1889.

                                        Thomas [his X mark] Flynn  (seal)

Signed, sealed and published in presence of:
  Bernard McGinley
  Owen Brennan

Proved and letters testamentary granted 2nd April 1889.

Will Book G, page 47. Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania.

In the name of God, Amen. I, HENRY SCHOENER, of the Township of Cass in the County of Schuylkill, being of sound mind and memory, do make this my last Will and Testament.

Item. I give unto my wife CATHARINE all my household goods and the income of my farm during her widowhood.

Item. I give unto my sons PETER and JACOB the farm whereon I now live, to be divided between them at the decease of my said wife.

Witness my hand and seal this ninth day of November, A.D. 1873.

                                        Henry Schoener  (seal)

Witnesses:
  Daniel Kaercher
  [illegible]

Proved 28th November 1873.

Thirteen other pages showed the same text, a 1873 will of a different man, which is odd and should be checked on the scan itself.

Next, the will page should be passed to the record reader to pull out its details, and the scan should be checked to confirm whether the Thomas Flynn in it is the father in the tree.

Would you like me to pass the will page to the record reader next?

In the name of God, Amen. I, THOMAS FLYNN, of the Borough of Minersville in the County of Schuylkill and State of Pennsylvania, being weak in body but of sound mind, memory and understanding, do make and publish this my last Will and Testament.

Item. I give and bequeath unto my beloved wife MARGARET FLYNN the dwelling house and lot whereon I now reside, for and during the term of her natural life.

Item. I give unto my son JOHN FLYNN the sum of one hundred dollars.

Item. I give unto my daughter MARY ANN DOUGHERTY, wife of Patrick Dougherty, the sum of one hundred dollars.

Item. The residue of my estate I direct to be sold and divided equally among my children aforesaid.

I appoint my wife Margaret Flynn and my friend JAMES CONNELL executors of this my last Will.

In witness whereof I have hereunto set my hand and seal this fourteenth day of March, A.D. 1889.

                                        Thomas [his X mark] Flynn  (seal)

Signed, sealed and published in presence of:
  Bernard McGinley
  Owen Brennan

Proved and letters testamentary granted 2nd April 1889.
